newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn sharply higher on dry Midwest weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn sharply higher on dry Midwest weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were sharply higher early Monday, rallying on reports of hot and dry weather in the U.S. Midwest over the weekend, traders said.
"We are sharply higher because no rain means no grain," said one floor trader.
Also, extreme heat can hamper the pollination process in corn. Most corn in the U.S. Midwest pollinates in July.
The key crop area in central Illinois did not receive rain over the weekend, where it is badly needed, traders said.
U.S. forecasters said that most of the rain that fell over the weekend landed in the northern part of the Midwest.
Some forecasts show that there is a slight chance of rain for central Illinois on Monday.
The dry weather pushed December and September corn up the daily 12-cent-per-bushel trading limit near the open.
In early trade, Prudential Securities bought two million bushels September, Griffin Trading bought two million December and Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov sold one million September, traders said.
At 1002 CDT, September corn was 9-1/4 cents a bushel higher at $2.46 per bushel, and other months were 6-1/2 to 8-3/4 higher.
